newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expected to visit tornado-struck Arkansas.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expected to visit tornado-struck Arkansas.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was expected to declare a disaster area in parts of Arkansas struck by deadly tornadoes and to visit his home state on Tuesday, a White House official said on Sunday.

The official, who asked not to be identifed, said Clinton had to wait for the state to make a formal request for such federal aid before he could declare a disaster area, adding that this was likely to occur later on Sunday.
Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee said the series of storms on Saturday killed 23 people and injured hundreds of others, figures not immediately confirmed by federal officials.
"It's a major disaster. That's the simplest way to put it," said Ray Briggler of the Arkansas Office of Emergency Services. Briggler also said he could not confirm the governor's death count.

Clinton on Sunday returned to Washington from New York, where he celebrated his daughter Chelsea's 17th birthday. White House spokesman David Johnson said he had spoken with Federal Emergency Management Agency Director James Lee Witt from New York on Saturday night about the situation in his home state.
"The president is quite concerned with the situation," Johnson said, adding that Clinton first learned of the tornado as he arrived to attend the show "Chicago" in New York.

Separately, the White House official said Clinton was expected to postpone a news conference he had scheduled for Tuesday until later in the week, probably until Friday, in order to make the trip to Arkansas.
Witt is to travel to Arkansas as early as Sunday to help coordinate relief for victims of the tornado, he added.
Several hospitals in south and central Arkansas reported treating scores of storm-related injuries, many of them serious.
In some areas, electrical power and telephone service was lost when uprooted trees snapped utility lines. "It's a mess," said Sgt. George Craig of the Pulaski County sheriff's department.
Huckabee activated units of the Arkansas National Guard to maintain order and assist in proving emergency services.

The hardest hit area appeared to be Arkadelphia, a small city about 50 miles (80 km) southwest of Little Rock, where three fatalities occurred. Dozens of homes and some businesses were heavily damaged or destroyed.
Two others were killed in adjoining Saline County and a sixth in Jackson County, about 150 miles (240 km) to the northeast.
No dollar estimate on the damage was available.
"We're concerned about people right now, not money," said the governor's press secretary. "I expect the governor will be declaring at least three counties disaster areas later tonight."
The tornadoes were accompanied by extremely heavy rains and marble-sized hail.

"We heard the weather sirens go off and went outside and we could see it coming," said Kim Switlik, who was with her family in their suburban Little Rock home, which was heavily damaged. "We ran to the bathroom and covered our heads with pillows and started praying."
